prompts_findings.prompt_lead: Name the top five hooks you see people actually using with Claude Code, beyond formatting and linting.

risks_fired.evidence: "Cross-reference each with this repo: the event it fires on, and the specific file, convention, or failure mode here it would catch" (line 18 of the expanded fence) asks for five repo-grounded specifics with no explicit verify-or-quote-the-line clause -- check_prompts.md #13(b)'s own prescribed fix for this exact pattern ("quote the sentence in cited file that supports it; if you can't find one, mark [CITATION UNSUPPORTED]"). Mitigating but not neutralising: this runs inside a live agentic Claude Code session with full tool access to the actual repo (not an offline citation task), and the repo genuinely has real hook config to find (check_prompts.md #22 names `.claude/hooks/prompt-edit-gate.sh` and `.githooks/pre-commit` as this repo's own PreToolUse/pre-commit hooks), so a well-behaved run has real material to ground on without inventing. "No preamble. List them." optimises for a terse final answer, which could suppress the visible grep/read narration a careful run would otherwise show, but does not itself stop the tool calls from happening first. Confidence stays low (catalog band: "allows but scaffold mitigates; <30%") because the scaffold here is Claude Code's own default tool-using behaviour, not anything the prompt text itself supplies.

Repo-grounded specifics requested with no explicit verify-first clause; see prompts_findings for full evidence, mitigation, and fix_hint.
